gen-gf-halant-work-sans: Halant has a literary hush, with small letters nearly as tall as its capitals. Work Sans follows in sans-serif form, its strokes uniform and modern, so the page moves from a lightly shaded heading to text with no variation in stroke thickness.
gen-gf-hanuman-fs-ranade: Hanuman puts big, bookish lowercase up front, with openings that stay generous even in heavy weights. And Ranade does the gentler job, its sans strokes shifting only slightly and its letters spread far apart.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-fs-karma: Karma is a trustworthy serif with terminals that stop well short of the stem. Happy Monkey brings bold display character above it, its lines ruler-straight and its e wide open, while the serif text underneath keeps a quiet modulation.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-fs-roundo: Roundo has a lowercase n whose arch and stem match, and tiny counters that never clog. And Happy Monkey brings the swagger: ruler-straight lines and wide-gapped e shapes, a bold display voice sitting over that tidy plain sans.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-line-seed-jp: LINE Seed JP draws its horizontals exactly as heavy as its verticals, with counters that let the eye slip in and out. Happy Monkey is the loud one, bold and ruler-straight.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-special-gothic: Happy Monkey is bold and distinctive, its round letters drawn like bent wire, with wide gaps in the e. Special Gothic brings low, rounded sans forms that stay open and inviting, and that softness is the pair's best trait.
gen-gf-kadwa-fs-ranade: Traditional in mood, Kadwa starts with a first capital that barely rises above its neighbors. But Ranade's thick strokes lead the eye without dominating it, and its widely spaced sans letters would let a long passage drift along.
gen-gf-kosugi-maru-fs-literata: Literata is a sturdy serif, bookish, with wide-mouthed curves. Kosugi Maru sits above it in a fixed-width nib line, so its connected counters and drafting-pen outlines contrast with the slightly thinner joins in the text.
gen-gf-libertinus-mono-archivo: Archivo has a commanding x-height and curves that open outward instead of curling in, giving it an editorial lean. Libertinus Mono, with its pressed-glass bowls above, makes the reading feel steady.
gen-gf-libertinus-mono-fs-ranade: Ranade is a sans-serif whose weight shifts like stretched rubber cord, only slightly. Libertinus Mono, tall and pen-nib shaped, makes the sharpest difference, its structure set against that loose, spread-out line.
